story: DF2.7 - Session-Cumulative Cost Instrumentation in the Team Lead Driver
note: This artifact records THREE separate invocations of the same code at the same working tree, each labelled with its own command. They are not one run presented as one: the harness does not persist the driver's raw stdout, so the raw NDJSON is captured from a direct driver invocation of the same code path the harness spawns (buildTeamSpawn returns exactly `bun cli-anything/scripts/team-lead-driver.ts`).

providerFidelity.reason: No provider credential exists on this host: ~/.pi/agent/auth.json is empty ([]) and OPENROUTER_API_KEY is unset. R5 sec6 fact 4 already records the Anthropic OAuth expiry (~2026-02-25). A live smoke:team would fail at auth and spend nothing, so it could not produce a usage-bearing stream at all.
providerFidelity.substitute: cli-anything/test/fixtures/team-bin/pi - a shim that replays a REAL-shaped pi --mode json NDJSON stream. Every other component on the path is production code: runner.ts -> buildTeamSpawn -> team-lead-driver.ts -> cost events -> parseTeamEventLine -> the budget guard.
providerFidelity.whatThisDoesAndDoesNotProve: PROVES: the instrumentation is session-cumulative end to end, survives pi's duplicate message_update/turn_end/agent_end emissions, and flows into the budget guard. DOES NOT PROVE: any dollar figure against a real provider bill - the token and cost numbers below are replayed, not billed.

usageShapeProvenance.source: 17 real pi assistant-message usage records read from ~/.pi/agent/sessions (1465 usage records scanned across 10 session directories), plus pi's own dist/core/usage-totals.js
usageShapeProvenance.cacheFieldSpelling: camelCase - cacheRead / cacheWrite. NOT cache_read_input_tokens / cache_creation_input_tokens.
usageShapeProvenance.cacheFieldsObserved: 0 in every one of the 1465 records scanned. Emitted as reported (0); never synthesized from residuals, so gates report sec3.4 condition 2 stays open.
usageShapeProvenance.perFieldMode: PER-TURN DELTA for all five fields (input, output, cacheRead, cacheWrite, cost.total). Decisive evidence: pi derives session totals by SUMMING per-message usage - addUsageToTotals(totals, usage) { totals.input += usage.input; ...; totals.cost += usage.cost.total } in dist/core/usage-totals.js. Corroborated observationally: per-record output is non-monotone across a session (158, 333, 799, 452, 200, 145), which a running total cannot be.
usageShapeProvenance.operatorChosen: accumulate (+=), applied once per assistant message_end
usageShapeProvenance.probeDeviation: The story's live two-leg probe could not be run (no credential - see providerFidelity). Substituted: pi's own accumulation source plus the real local session corpus. The verdict is per-field and empirical either way; the recorded gap is that no leg ran against a BILLED stream, and that every observed record priced at $0 (OAuth/free routing), so cost.total's delta semantics rest on the source reading rather than on observed non-zero values.
usageShapeProvenance.versionCorrection: A bare shell `pi` on this host is the GLOBAL @earendil-works build (0.84.1), which is where the session corpus and the first source reading came from. But `bun run`/`npm run` prepend node_modules/.bin, so every project script — smoke:team, and therefore the driver's spawn('pi') — gets the WORKSPACE-PINNED @mariozechner/pi-coding-agent 0.55.0, the F13 pin. There is no version deviation on the code path. Re-verified directly against 0.55.0: Usage is field-for-field identical (camelCase cacheRead/cacheWrite, cost.total), and 0.55.0 likewise derives session totals by summing per-assistant-message usage (agent-session.js:2205-2215). The per-turn-delta verdict holds on BOTH builds.
usageShapeProvenance.residualRisk: readTurnUsage treats an absent or malformed cost block as UNPRICED rather than as $0. Every record in the observed corpus carries a cost block (total 0), so this is the shape pi emits even for unpriced routing - but it was not confirmed against a :free OpenRouter slug specifically. If some provider omits the block entirely, those turns count as unpriced and the run degrades to a mechanical merge rather than over-reporting spend. That is the fail-closed direction INV-COST-5 asks for.

doubleCountHazardFound: pi emits the SAME assistant message object - carrying the SAME usage - on message_start, every message_update, message_end and turn_end, and replays the whole message list in agent_end. A naive += over every usage-bearing event multiplies the bill several-fold and would kill healthy runs early at the budget guard (INV-COST-3). Usage is therefore accumulated on message_end ONLY, and toolResult messages are excluded (pi documents their usage as 'not part of main LLM context accounting').
truncatedStreamHazardFound: Accumulating on message_end alone drops an in-flight turn when the timeout path SIGKILLs pi mid-message - and, worse, would emit that truncated record as COMPLETE. The harvest therefore tracks the open message and counts an unterminated one as turnCount+1 / unpricedTurns+1, so the runaway-worker case (the expensive one) marks the total partial instead of failing open.

resetBoundary.contract: the pi subprocess invocation; each runWorkerPi call starts its accumulators at zero
resetBoundary.leg2Finding: pi --mode json subscribes to LIVE session events only (modes/print-mode.js: session.subscribe -> toJsonEvent) and does not replay pre-existing session entries as they happen. A resumed --session-id therefore emits only its own new turns; no carried-in baseline needs subtracting.
resetBoundary.noSessionNote: The driver spawns pi with --no-session, so a resumed --session-id is unreachable on this code path today. The fixtures encode the boundary anyway because it is the contract DF2.8's ledger sums over, not because the shipped driver can currently enter it.
resetBoundary.negativeControlEncoded: pi-session-resume-b.ndjson's agent_end message list replays the earlier invocation's messages, so the carried-in totals are physically present in the stream. An implementation that reads them restates leg A's spend inside leg B's cost event, the two events sum to 37000 input tokens / $0.072 instead of the true 26000 / $0.052, and DF2.8's ledger SUM bills the first invocation twice. SCOPE OF THIS CONTROL, stated honestly: it kills an agent_end-list accumulator. It does NOT exercise the spec's other hypothesised hazard - pi reporting RUNNING totals across a resumed session, which would need baseline subtraction - because the probe found per-turn deltas, so no such stream can be produced and no baseline-subtraction code exists to test.

3_unpricedDriverRun.command: PATH=... QDS_FAKE_PI_UNPRICED=1 QDS_AGENT_TEAM_CONFIG_JSON=<1-worker config> bun cli-anything/scripts/team-lead-driver.ts
3_unpricedDriverRun.purpose: INV-COST-5 demonstration - the middle turn's usage block is absent
3_unpricedDriverRun.reading: turnCount 3, unpricedTurns 1, costUsd 0.0464772 = the two priced turns only. The unmeasured turn was never priced at $0 and never credited against the total.
3_unpricedDriverRun.nextPaidSubprocessRefused: The LEAD MERGE, specifically. Workers are dispatched concurrently under Promise.all, so the lead merge is the only paid subprocess the driver can still refuse once a worker's partiality is known. This is not a general per-turn kill - that needs the engine-side projection DF3.6 owns.
3_unpricedDriverRun.blastRadius: The guard is per-RUN: one partial worker refuses the merge for the whole run, including for healthy workers, because the cumulative total the budget guard reads is per-run. A worker SIGKILLed on the PI_COMS_TIMEOUT_MS path now counts as partial, so routine timeouts degrade the run to a mechanical merge. Regression-locked by a multi-worker test.
stderr: team-lead-driver: refusing paid lead merge: cumulative cost is partial (unpriced turns from worker-a); falling back to concat
3_unpricedDriverRun.harnessSide: runner.ts sets costUnpriced on the budget state and reports it in every error detail that carries cumulativeCostUsd. GAP, stated: on the SUCCESS path runTeamManifest reports no cost figure at all, so it reports no partiality flag either - MergedOutput's key set is frozen by the P0.3-M2 uniform-schema contract (asserted by expectUniformSchema) and this story does not widen it. runTeamManifest also consumes cost events without persisting them. The machine-readable surface DF2.8 consumes is the driver's own NDJSON cost event stream, which carries turnCount and unpricedTurns on every event; persisting it is DF2.8's ledger work and is out of scope here per the story's Trigger Surface.

comparisonToF6LastTurnSum.f6Semantics: LAST-TURN sum. F6's own measurementCaveat: 'team-lead-driver.ts harvests usage from the LAST pi message event per worker (runWorkerPi overwrite semantics), so multi-turn worker sessions under-report'. Attempt 2's true cost was left bracketed [$0.049, ~$0.91].
comparisonToF6LastTurnSum.instrumentedSemantics: SESSION-CUMULATIVE sum across all turns of each pi invocation
comparisonToF6LastTurnSum.notComparableAsDollars: F6 ran real providers; this rerun replays a stub. The comparison below is of SEMANTICS, not of bills.

semanticDemonstration.reading: On this 3-turn stream the pre-change assignment implementation reports 30.9% of the real spend. F6's $0.04912262 is the same kind of number: a floor, not a total. The bracket F6 left open is exactly what this instrumentation closes.

hazard3_toolOutputAsReply: Text blocks were harvested from every message-bearing event, including toolResult. A run ending on a tool result handed the tool's output to extractJsonObject; if that output was itself JSON it was emitted verbatim as the worker's structured worker_output, changedFiles and all - untrusted tool content promoted to a worker result. Text collection is now gated on the same assistant-role predicate as usage. Regression-locked by a test verified to fail when the gate is removed.
